title: Efficacy of the pentavalent rotavirus vaccine, RotaTeq®, in Finnish infants up to 3 years of age: the Finnish Extension Study.
ehr_evidence: Monitoring for health care encounters in FES followed the same approach that was used to monitor infants in REST... episodes of AGE requiring hospitalisation or an ED visit were collected at prespecified 12-week intervals by automated short message service contacts, sent via mobile phones, or by direct telephone calls... Case report forms in FES were modelled after the case report forms in REST
summary: Extension study (FES) evaluating the sustained efficacy of the pentavalent rotavirus vaccine (RV5) against rotavirus gastroenteritis and acute gastroenteritis hospitalizations and ED visits in Finnish infants up to 3.1 years post-vaccination.
key_findings: RV5 reduced RVGE hospitalizations and ED visits by 93.8% (95% CI: 90.8–95.9%) over up to 3.1 years.

Vaccine efficacy against combined hospitalizations and ED visits was 93.9% (95% CI: 89.1–96.9%) in children 4-11 months, 94.4% (95% CI: 90.2–97.0%) in 12-23 months, and 85.9% (95% CI: 51.6–97.2%) in 24-35 months.
RV5 reduced all-cause acute gastroenteritis hospitalizations and ED visits by 62.4% (95% CI: 57.6–66.6%).
Efficacy against G1 rotavirus was 95.3% (95% CI: 92.5–97.2%), but results for G4 were not significant due to low case numbers.
No cases of intussusception were observed during the FES period.
captured_features: rotavirus genotypes (G1, G2, G3, G4, G9)
study_design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (extension study)
population: Finnish infants enrolled at 6-13 weeks of age, followed up to 3.1 years post-vaccination
limitations: Small number of cases in year 3 limiting statistical power
Too few encounters for G2 and G4 serotypes to demonstrate significant efficacy
Wide confidence intervals for efficacy beyond 24 months
Variation in follow-up duration due to rolling enrollment
